destinations.name: Qutub Minar
destinations.price_level: Moderate (INR 550 for Foreigners, INR 40 for Indians)
destinations.opening_hours: Sunrise to Sunset (approx. 7:00 AM - 6:00 PM), Open all 7 days
destinations.description: A 73-meter tall red sandstone minaret built by Qutb-ud-din Aibak in 1192. The complex features the famous 4th-century rust-resistant Iron Pillar of Chandragupta II and ornate Indo-Islamic carvings.
destinations.transport: Take the Delhi Metro Yellow Line and alight at Qutub Minar Metro Station. From there, take an electric auto-rickshaw or walk 1.2 km.
destinations.etiquette: Modest clothing recommended. Tripods require prior ASI authorization. Avoid touching the ancient carved stone surfaces.
destinations.emergency: Tourist Police Kiosk located near the main ticket counter. Nearest hospital: Max Super Speciality Hospital Saket (3 km).

destinations.name: Red Fort (Lal Qila)
destinations.price_level: Moderate (INR 550 for Foreigners, INR 50 for Indians)
destinations.opening_hours: 9:30 AM to 4:30 PM, Closed on Mondays
destinations.description: Constructed in 1639 by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan as the palace of his fortified capital Shahjahanabad. Known for its massive red sandstone walls, Diwan-i-Aam, and Diwan-i-Khas.
destinations.transport: Delhi Metro Violet Line to Lal Quila Station (Gate 4 exits right in front of the fort) or Yellow Line to Chandni Chowk.
destinations.etiquette: Expect security bag screening. Drones and large backpacks are prohibited. Evening Light and Sound show is available in English and Hindi.
destinations.emergency: Kotwali Police Station Old Delhi (0.8 km). Sanjeevan Hospital Daryaganj (1.5 km).

destinations.name: Humayun's Tomb
destinations.price_level: Moderate (INR 550 for Foreigners, INR 40 for Indians)
destinations.opening_hours: 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM, Open all days
destinations.description: Built in 1570, this garden tomb inspired the Taj Mahal. Represents the earliest example of grand Mughal Charbagh garden architecture in India.
destinations.transport: Delhi Metro Violet Line to JLN Stadium Station, then a 5-minute auto-rickshaw ride (approx. INR 50-80).
destinations.etiquette: Quiet atmosphere; do not climb on fragile marble plinths. Sunrise and golden hour are prime times for photography.
destinations.emergency: Hazrat Nizamuddin Police Station (0.5 km). Moolchand Hospital (3.5 km).

destinations.name: Gurudwara Bangla Sahib
destinations.description: One of the most prominent Sikh gurdwaras in India, associated with the eighth Sikh Guru, Guru Har Krishan. Features a holy pond (Sarovar) and a massive 24/7 community kitchen (Langar) serving over 30,000 free meals daily.
destinations.transport: Metro Blue/Yellow Line to Rajiv Chowk or Patel Chowk, then a 10-minute walk or cycle rickshaw.
destinations.etiquette: Mandatory head covering (scarves provided free at the entrance). Remove shoes and wash hands/feet at the foot-washing pool before entering. Strictly no tobacco, alcohol, or leather belts inside sanctum.
destinations.emergency: On-site charitable dispensary open 24/7. Connaught Place Police Station (1 km).

destinations.name: Taj Mahal
destinations.type: Seven Wonders of the World / UNESCO
destinations.price_level: Premium (INR 1100 + 200 for main mausoleum for foreigners; INR 50 for Indians)
destinations.opening_hours: Sunrise to Sunset (approx. 6:00 AM - 6:30 PM). STRICTLY CLOSED ON FRIDAYS.
destinations.description: An ivory-white marble mausoleum commissioned in 1632 by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan to house the tomb of his favorite wife, Mumtaz Mahal. Regarded as the jewel of Muslim art in India.
destinations.transport: From Delhi, take the Gatimaan Express (1h 40m) or Vande Bharat Express to Agra Cantt railway station. From Agra Cantt, electric golf carts and battery autos shuttle to the East/West gates (pollution-free zone).
destinations.etiquette: No food, lighters, cigarettes, chewing gum, tripods, or drone equipment allowed. Shoe covers must be worn when climbing onto the marble terrace (provided with ticket).
destinations.emergency: Agra Tourist Police Station located at Taj East Gate (Phone: +91 562 242 1204). S.N. Medical College Hospital (4 km).

destinations.name: Agra Fort
destinations.price_level: Moderate (INR 550 for Foreigners, INR 40 for Indians)
destinations.description: The imperial residence of the Mughal dynasty until 1638. Houses Jahangir Palace, Khas Mahal, and the Musamman Burj tower where Shah Jahan was imprisoned by his son Aurangzeb with a distant view of the Taj.
destinations.transport: Located 2.5 km northwest of the Taj Mahal. Electric autos connect the two monuments in 10 minutes (approx. INR 80-100).
destinations.etiquette: Expect monkey activity in open gardens—do not carry open food packets or eat in the open corridors.
destinations.emergency: Rakabganj Police Station (1.2 km). District Hospital Agra (2 km).

destinations.name: Amber Palace (Amer Fort)
destinations.price_level: Moderate (INR 500 for Foreigners, INR 100 for Indians)
destinations.opening_hours: 8:00 AM to 5:30 PM (Day visit), 6:30 PM to 9:15 PM (Night Fort visit)
destinations.description: Majestic fort situated atop Cheel ka Teela (Hill of Eagles) overlooking Maota Lake. Famous for its Sheesh Mahal (Mirror Palace) where mirrors glitter from candle reflections, Jai Mandir, and royal courtyards.
destinations.transport: Bus #29 from Jaipur Hawa Mahal or AC low-floor bus #5. Private auto/cab takes 25 minutes from the Old Pink City.
destinations.etiquette: Wear comfortable walking shoes with good grip on stone inclines. Licensed guides wear government badges with fixed tariff rates.
destinations.emergency: Amer Police Station at fort foot (Phone: 0141-2530122). Sawai Man Singh (SMS) Hospital in Jaipur (11 km).

destinations.name: Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds)
destinations.price_level: Budget (INR 200 for Foreigners, INR 50 for Indians)
destinations.opening_hours: 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM, Open all days
destinations.description: Built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh. Its five-story exterior resembles a honeycomb with 953 small jharokhas (casements) that allowed royal women to observe street festivals without being seen.
destinations.transport: Located directly inside the Pink City market on Badi Chaupar. Best reached on foot from City Palace or by auto-rickshaw.
destinations.etiquette: Best frontal photos are taken from the rooftop cafes directly across the road (Tattoo Cafe or Wind View Cafe) during morning sunlight.
destinations.emergency: Manak Chowk Police Station (200m). SMS Hospital Jaipur (3 km).

destinations.name: City Palace Jaipur
destinations.price_level: Moderate to Premium (INR 700 standard foreign ticket; INR 2500 royal quarters)
destinations.opening_hours: 9:30 AM to 5:00 PM, Evening tour 7:00 PM to 10:00 PM
destinations.description: The seat of the Maharaja of Jaipur, featuring courtyards, gardens, and buildings that blend Rajput and Mughal architecture. Includes the famous Peacock Gate (Pritam Niwas Chowk).
destinations.transport: Adjacent to Jantar Mantar and Hawa Mahal in the center of the Old City. Walking distance from Badi Chaupar.
destinations.etiquette: Photography is restricted in certain royal museum galleries. Audio guides in English, French, German, and Spanish are available at the courtyard counter.

destinations.name: Dashashwamedh Ghat & Ganga Aarti
destinations.price_level: Free public access (Boat ride: INR 200-500 per person)
destinations.opening_hours: Open 24 hours. Grand evening Aarti begins daily around 6:45 PM (summer) / 6:00 PM (winter)
destinations.description: The main and most vibrant ghat on the Ganges River in Varanasi. Every evening, young Hindu priests perform a choreographic ritual with tiered brass lamps, conch shells, and incense worshiping Mother Ganga.
destinations.transport: Vehicles are stopped at Godowlia Chowk. From Godowlia, walk 500 meters down through the vibrant bazaar to the river steps.
destinations.etiquette: Be respectful of prayers. You can watch from the ghat steps or book a wooden rowing boat. Avoid aggressive hawkers selling flower lamps (diyas). Do NOT photograph cremation pyres at nearby Manikarnika Ghat.
destinations.emergency: Dashashwamedh Police Station (400m). Heritage Hospital Lanka (4 km).

destinations.name: Paranthe Wali Gali
destinations.description: Historic alleyway in Chandni Chowk famous since the 1870s for shallow-fried stuffed Indian flatbreads (paranthas) with fillings ranging from spiced potato and paneer to banana and rabri, served with sweet pumpkin and tamarind chutney.
destinations.transport: Chandni Chowk Metro Station (Yellow Line), Gate 5. Take an electric rickshaw into Dariba Kalan / Kinari Bazaar.
destinations.etiquette: Pure vegetarian establishments. Cash and UPI payments preferred; foreign credit cards rarely accepted in small alley shops.

destinations.name: Karim's Historic Mughlai Dining
destinations.description: Established in 1913 near Jama Masjid by Haji Karimuddin, a former royal chef to the Mughal Emperor. Renowned for Mutton Korma, Chicken Jahangiri, Seekh Kebabs, and freshly baked Tandoori Roti.
destinations.transport: Jama Masjid Metro Station (Violet Line), Gate 1, walk 200 meters into Gali Kababian.
destinations.etiquette: Halal certified. Expect weekend waiting queues. Dress conservatively when passing through Jama Masjid lanes.

destinations.name: Laxmi Misthan Bhandar (LMB)
destinations.description: Established in 1727 in Johari Bazaar. Famous for authentic Rajasthani Royal Thali (Dal Baati Churma, Gatte ki Sabzi, Ker Sangri) and famous sweets like Paneer Ghewar.
destinations.transport: Located directly on Johari Bazaar road in Pink City. Walkable from Badi Chaupar Metro Station.
destinations.etiquette: Pure vegetarian, highly clean and foreign-tourist friendly with air-conditioned dining hall.

destinations.name: Temple and Religious Customs Guide
destinations.description: Crucial customs: 1) Always remove shoes and socks before entering any Hindu temple, Sikh Gurudwara, or Jain shrine. 2) Cover shoulders, cleavage, and knees. 3) In Sikh Gurudwaras, both men and women must cover their heads. 4) Use your right hand when receiving holy prasad or giving offerings. 5) Walk clockwise (pradakshina) around shrines.
destinations.etiquette: Ask permission before taking photos of devotees or sanctum deities; photography inside inner sanctums (Garbhagriha) is strictly prohibited.
destinations.emergency: Tourist Police Helpline: Dial 1363 (24/7 toll-free multilingual support).

destinations.name: Delhi Metro Tourist Smart Card & Transport Guide
destinations.price_level: Budget (INR 200 for 1-day pass, INR 500 for 3-day pass with unlimited rides)
destinations.opening_hours: Trains run 6:00 AM to 11:00 PM daily
destinations.description: The Delhi Metro is world-class, fully air-conditioned, fast, and safe. The Tourist Card allows unlimited rides on all network lines except Airport Express. The first coach of every train traveling in moving direction is strictly reserved for women.
destinations.transport: Buy tourist cards at customer care counters of any metro station, including Terminal 3 IGI Airport Metro.
destinations.etiquette: Eating, drinking, and chewing gum on trains or platform areas is penalized. Stand on the left of escalators.
destinations.emergency: Delhi Metro 24/7 Helpline: 155370. CISF Metro Security: 155655.

destinations.name: National Emergency SOS & Tourist Security
destinations.description:
Immediate Emergency Numbers in India: 
• Unified Emergency (Police, Fire, Ambulance): 112
• Ministry of Tourism 24x7 Multilingual Helpline: 1363 or 1800-11-1363 (English, Hindi, French, Spanish, German, Japanese, Russian, Italian, Mandarin)
• Women's Safety Helpline: 1091
• Ambulance: 102 or 108
• Cyber Crime Portal: 1930
destinations.transport: Emergency vehicles have right of way.
destinations.etiquette: If filing an e-FIR for lost property (phone/passport), visit the nearest Tourist Police Booth to receive a formal stamped non-cognizable report for your embassy and travel insurer.
